Tactical mechanics dictate that forms of struggle
must match the flow and ebb of the revolution.
Offensive Tactics: During a rising tide, tactics must be aggressively revolutionar
• Forms: General political strikes, open demonstrations, armed uprisings
Defensive Tactics: During a declining tide, tactics must pivot
to organized retreat and accumulation of forces.
• Forms: Cultural/educational work, partial economic strikes,
participation in bourgeois parliaments (the Duma).

The Party as Vanguard: Directing the struggle
versus dragging at its tail.
Khvostism (Tailism)
The Vanguard
The Error of Spontaneity: The ideology of trade-unionism
and opportunism dictates that the party should merely heed
the spontaneous labor movement. This surrenders the
working class to bourgeois hegemony.
The Leninist General Staff: The Party must be armed with
revolutionary theory to see further than the working class. It
must overcome the inertia of the spontaneous movement and
raise the masses to the level of class consciousness.

The Transmission Belt Model of Proletarian Organization.
Olanguard is nourization.
The Party is the highest form of class organization, but it is numerically small. It operates by centralizing leadership through
non-party mass organizations, transforming them into "transmission belts" that link the Party's will to the working class.
- The Engine: The Vanguard
Party (General Staff)
- Transmission Belts:
Trade Unions, Co-operatives,
Soviets, Youth Leaques
The Wheels: The Proletarian Class and Reserves

From Theory to State Apparatus.
By systematizing Lenin's sprawling actions
into this rigid, replicable science of
revolution, the foundations were laid for the
ideological machinery of the 20th century.
It transformed Marxism from a theoretical
critique of capitalism into a ruthless, highly
organized methodology for dismantling
states and engineering new ones.
